meta.title: First week at Saltmarsh
meta.kicker: Saltmarsh Coffee Roasters · New starter handbook
meta.dek: Welcome. This is the handbook every new roaster and barista reads in their first week: how a green seed becomes the cup you hand across the counter, how to pull a shot inside the window, what to do each day, and five questions to answer before your first solo shift.
byline: For new roastery and cafe staff
Demonstration: Saltmarsh, its people and every figure here are invented
meta.description: An illustrated first-week handbook for new staff at an invented coffee roaster, with a bean-to-cup flow, a sourcing map, a shot-timing drill, a checklist and a quiz.

roastery.alt: Watercolor of a coffee roastery in the morning: a teal drum roaster with a copper hopper and chimney, a chute pouring into a cooling tray of dark beans, two burlap sacks of green coffee labeled Ethiopia and Colombia, a packed bag of Saltmarsh coffee, a cup with a latte-art heart and a chalkboard of today's roasts.

hero.caption: The roastery at seven in the morning: the drum warming, the first sacks open, the first bag of the day packed.

blocks.text:
Saltmarsh roasted its first batch in a rented garage in {{company.founded|year}}. {{company.years}} later it runs {{company.cafes}} and a roastery, and {{company.staff}} work here. Everything we serve still starts on the same floor: the green coffee comes in by the sack, goes through the drum, rests, and leaves in a bag with a roast date on it.

This week you will work every station once. Nobody expects you to be fast. We expect you to taste everything and to ask why.
Taste it before you serve it. If you would not drink it, pour it out and pull another one.

chapters.title: Every cup starts as a green seed

blocks.text: A coffee bean is the seed of a fruit. It reaches us green and smelling of grass; the drum turns it brown, sweet and brittle. Six steps sit between the farm and the cup, and you will touch the last three every shift.

blocks.title: From green seed to your cup
blocks.subtitle: Select a step for what happens there and who does it.

nodes.label: Source
nodes.text: We cup every lot before we buy it and buy only what scores {{brew.cupping_bar}} or more.

nodes.label: Roast
nodes.text: {{company.batches_week}} a week, each logged by the roaster's controller.

nodes.label: Rest
nodes.text: Fresh roasts give off gas for days. Espresso waits at least {{brew.rest_days}} after roasting.

nodes.label: Grind
nodes.text: Grind for each shot, never ahead: ground coffee goes stale in minutes.

nodes.label: Brew
nodes.text: A double shot takes {{brew.dose}} of coffee and yields {{brew.yield}} of espresso, a ratio of {{brew.ratio}}.

nodes.label: Serve
nodes.text: Taste a sip from a spoon before the cup goes across the counter.

blocks.title: Where this year's coffee comes from
blocks.subtitle: Green coffee bought for 2026 by origin, kilograms. Tiles sit roughly where the countries are.
blocks.caption: {{company.origins}} in all, {{origins.total_kg}} of green coffee.

blocks.text: Every morning the first barista on shift dials in the grinder: pulls a shot, times it, tastes it and adjusts. Too fast and the coffee is thin and sour; too slow and it turns heavy and bitter. Grind finer to slow a shot down, coarser to speed it up.

blocks.name: dial-in
blocks.title: Dial in a shot
blocks.subtitle: Move the grinder setting until the shot lands in the window. A practice model: real coffee also changes with the bean, the roast date and the weather.
blocks.fallback: Grind finer to slow a shot, coarser to speed it up. A good double shot runs {{brew.time_low|plain}} to {{brew.time_high}}.

blocks.title: House rule
blocks.text: Change one thing at a time: the grind, then the dose, never both. Taste after every change.
Each day you shadow one station and then run it with your mentor beside you. Tick things off as you go; the list stays in this browser.

questions.q: A shot runs fast and tastes sour. What do you change?
questions.explain: A fast, sour shot is under-extracted. A finer grind slows it down.

questions.q: How long must a roast rest before we use it for espresso?
questions.explain: At least {{brew.rest_days}}: fresh coffee gives off gas that makes espresso uneven.

questions.q: How much coffee goes into a double shot?
When do you grind coffee for espresso?
options: At the start of the shift
questions.explain: Ground coffee goes stale in minutes, so we grind for each shot.

questions.q: Before a drink goes across the counter you...
options: Taste a sip from a spoon
questions.explain: Taste it before you serve it. That is the house rule.
